ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Given a transverse harmonic wave propagating along the $x$-axis, with $A{=}10\mathrm{cm}$ in both figures. Figure 1 shows the waveform at $t=2\mathbf{s}$, and Figure 2 shows the vibration image of the particle at the abscissa $x=2m$.

1. What is the direction of wave propagation and the wave speed?
2. What is the $y$ coordinate of the mass element at the horizontal coordinate $x=3m$ at time $t=15\mathrm{s}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Propagating in the negative direction of the $x$-axis at $1\mathrm{m/s}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given a transverse harmonic wave propagating along the $x$-axis, with $A=10\mathrm{cm}$ in both figures. Figure 1 shows the waveform at $t=2\mathrm{s}$, and Figure 2 shows the vibration image of the particle at the abscissa $x=2\mathrm{m}$. 1. What is the direction of wave propagation and the wave speed? 2. What is the $y$ coordinate of the mass element at the horizontal coordinate $x=3\mathrm{m}$ at time $t=15\mathrm{s}$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Propagating in the negative direction of the $x$-axis at $1\mathrm{m/s}$. 0
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In Figure 1, the vertical axis is y with amplitude markings +A and -A, and the horizontal axis is x in meters. The wave profile shown for t=2 s crosses y=0 at about x=0, 2, 4, and 6 m, has crests at about x=1 m and x=5 m, and has a trough at about x=3 m. Thus the wavelength read from the spatial graph is 4 m. In Figure 2, the vertical axis is y with the same amplitude markings, and the horizontal axis is t in seconds for the particle at x=2 m. The vibration graph crosses y=0 at about t=0, 2, 4, and 6 s, has crests at about t=1 s and t=5 s, and has a trough at about t=3 s. Thus the period is 4 s. Reasoning: From Figure 2, the particle at x=2 m was at a crest at t=1 s. One second later, at t=2 s, Figure 1 shows the corresponding nearest crest at x=1 m. Therefore that crest moved from x=2 m to x=1 m in 1 s, so the wave propagates in the negative x-direction. Its speed is distance/time = 1 m / 1 s = 1 m/s. This is consistent with v = wavelength/period = 4 m / 4 s = 1 m/s. For the displacement at x=3 m and t=15 s, compare with the known profile at t=2 s. The time difference is 15 s - 2 s = 13 s. Since the wave moves left at 1 m/s, the profile shifts left by 13 m, so y(3,15) equals the value in the t=2 s profile at x = 3 + 13 = 16 m. The wavelength is 4 m, so x=16 m is phase-equivalent to x=0 m in Figure 1. At x=0 m in Figure 1, y=0. Therefore y(3,15)=0.
